description: Test cases for validating the lecture-to-markdown-notes skill across different lecture types

evals.name: programming-oop-python
evals.topic: Object-Oriented Programming in Python: Classes and Objects
evals.description: Python lecture on classes, objects, inheritance, polymorphism with realistic code examples and common pitfalls
key_elements: Common pitfalls (mutable defaults, class vs instance attributes)
expected_output_features: Code blocks with Python syntax highlighting
Content reorganized logically from original lecture order

evals.name: stem-linear-algebra
evals.topic: Linear Algebra: Matrix Operations and Applications
evals.description: Mathematics lecture on matrix operations, determinants, inverses, eigenvalues, and real-world applications
key_elements: Applications in graphics and machine learning

evals.name: humanities-industrial-revolution
evals.topic: The Industrial Revolution: Social and Economic Transformation
evals.description: History lecture covering causes, key figures, technological innovations, and societal impacts of industrialization
key_elements: Key inventions (Spinning Jenny, Power Loom, Steam Engine)
Key figures (Hargreaves, Watt, Arkwright, Owen, Stephenson)
Rise of new classes (industrialists, middle class, working class)
expected_output_features: Timeline of key events and inventions
Multiple perspectives presented (factory owners vs workers)

general: All key concepts extracted and explained in clear, accessible language
Consistent hierarchy (H2 for sections, H3 for subsections, no level jumps)
Tables and code blocks used when relevant
Content reorganized logically, not in original lecture order
Notes are standalone (don't require referencing original source)
programming: Code examples use appropriate syntax highlighting
Concepts build logically from classes to inheritance to polymorphism
Common pitfalls and edge cases highlighted
humanities: Key figures and their roles highlighted

notes: These test cases are designed to be realistic lecture excerpts that test the skill's ability to handle different content types. They include natural lecture elements like tangents, repetition, varying detail levels, and conversational tone. The skill should reorganize, reformat, and structure them into clean, studyable notes.
